items.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
items.summary: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. items.title: OpenESM: Energy-Steered Models Are Scalable Foundation Learners
items.summary: Energy-based models have shown promising properties for domain-specific tasks but remain challenging in modeling general-purpose scenarios. To bridge this gap, we design energy-steered models (ESMs) for foundational language modeling. ESMs integrate energy steering and token generation within a single architecture to leverage the energy-guided search to refine token generation. items.summary: Large language models have shown outstanding performance on text-first tasks such as coding, math, and writing. items.summary: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds. items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agentic system to design, train, and evaluate its own successor. items.summary: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters. We explore an alternative: general-purpose coding agents that construct images through executable programs. items.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose language model activations into sparse features, but prompt transformations designed to preserve the underlying request can redistribute activity across them. A feature change observed on one transformed prompt need not recur, and even a recurring change need not affect a downstream computation. items.summary: For agentic data analysis, language-model agents often require a large number of annotated tasks to learn how to interact effectively with executable environments (i.e., databases). While high-quality annotated tasks require heavy manual effort, an executable environment already provides rich interaction structure and verifiable outcomes. items.summary: A fundamental challenge for explainable and accountable language models is revealing how external information influences their answers. This paper examines whether models are self-attributive: that is, whether they indicate when -- and only when -- their responses to questions are influenced by information provided alongside the question. items.summary: Agent harnesses enable large language models to act through tools, observe the results, and iteratively work toward a task goal. Verification checks and revises agents' work to improve output quality. Yet there is limited guidance on how harnesses should organize this effort. items.summary: Repeated attempts at interactive tasks uncover facts, useful operations, and failures that can inform subsequent execution. items.summary: An agent that truly knows and acts on behalf of its user has been a long-standing promise of AI assistants. Computer-use agents bring this promise within reach by capably executing fully specified tasks across apps. However, real-world user requests are often underspecified. items.summary: Catastrophic forgetting in continual learning (CL) manifests not only as accuracy degradation but also as explanation drift: models maintain predictive accuracy while silently shifting attention from diagnostic features to spurious correlations. items.summary: Online scene change detection requires integrating incoming observations to determine which regions have changed relative to a reference scene. items.summary: Animals have a remarkable capacity for autonomy---driven by intrinsic motivation---without external sensory cues or extrinsic objectives, yet the computational mechanisms behind this ability largely remain a mystery. items.summary: Harness self-evolution offers a practical route for LLM agents to improve from execution experience without updating model parameters. items.summary: Constrained decoding guarantees that Large Language Models (LLMs) produce outputs conforming to predefined formats, but is often assumed to inherently degrade reasoning. items.title: DeepSeek 开源看家算子的同一周，AI 超过了它
items.summary: 国产大模型的竞争，正从模型层延伸到算力层：再强的模型，最终都要基于算子在芯片上执行。同一个模型、同一块芯片，换一套更优的算子，有时会带来数倍的性能提升。算子的效率决定了同样的显卡能跑多快，也决定了每个 token 的价格。 DeepSeek 近日全面开源推理框架 DeepInfer。继模型权重和 FlashMLA、DeepGEMM 等算子库之后，他们把模型运行的链路开放了。其中的 FlashMLA，有工程师在芯片上逐行手调的版本，算子性能跑到了硬件极限的 90% 以上，这也是人类手艺目前在部分芯片上达到的极限成绩。 而这个极限，同一周就被 AI 刷新了。据悉，截至 10 月 22 日，完全由 AI 编写算子、无人工逐行调优的 ForgeKernel，同时登顶两个算子评测榜：英伟达主场的 SOL-ExecBench FlashInfer-Bench 合集第一，以及昇腾 CANN 官方仓库维护的 CANNBench A3 硬件榜第一，基准加速比 1.835×，领先第二名 25%。在名次之外，AI自主优化算子的能力不容小觑：在DeepSeek v4.1 Flash的算子上，相比DeepSeek开源的英伟达版本，ForgeKernel也通过从0用AI迭代的方式实现了性能超越。 这是智能进化的接力。无论是DeepSeek的开源精神还是算子优化榜单的焦灼竞争，最终都导向同一个方向：让国产智能在…
